messages:
samir: customer reported invoice (INV-2026-09) shows ~24k tokens but dashboard live-usage for the same period shows ~12.1k. They say discrepancy only happens for streaming endpoints when the client cancels mid-response.

marta: tagging @billing-ops and @eng-runtime — can you grab the request IDs and any metering logs?

samir: pasted the example request id they sent: req_0a9d3f2e. Customer says steps to repro: call streaming chat, wait ~1.8s into response, send client cancel (HTTP stream closed). Dashboard shows ~600 tokens for that request, invoice charged ~1.2k.

ian: curious — do they use automatic reconnect or an SSE proxy? That can cause the server to retry/duplicate chunks.

samir: they use a server-side SSE proxy in front of our API (nginx+lua). But they also mentioned sometimes they get a final small chunk repeated after reconnect.

support-bot: incident-log attached: events for req_0a9d3f2e -> stream_open, chunk_1(432 tokens), chunk_2(168 tokens), client_close, server_final_chunk(600 tokens), reconnection_attempt, server_final_chunk(600 tokens)

marta: if the final chunk appears twice in our billing events stream we could double-count. @ian can you confirm how metering dedup works for streaming?

ian: short answer: metering ties tokens to finished output events. For streaming we increment counts when the serving runtime writes a chunk to the SSE layer and emits metering events. If the runtime replays a final buffer on reconnect without de-duplicating request id + chunk index, billing can double-report. We're seeing one possible path: proxy closes socket -> client reconnects -> runtime replays final buffered tokens (same content) -> both write events emitted.

samir: customer included a minimal repro using curl + netcat to simulate midstream cancel. They said it reproduces locally ~7/10 runs. Repro steps they provided: 
```
# open SSE streaming request
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat -d '{"model":"rwd-4b","prompt":"long answer please"}' \
  | (sleep 1.8; pkill -f "curl -N" )
```
They then tail our metering events and see duplicate final chunk events.

marta: please attach the billing-event stream for req_0a9d3f2e and the dashboard usage log for the same window. We need to decide if invoice needs an adjustment now or after root-cause.

ian: pulling serving/runtime logs for that req: found two emit events: 
```
EMIT_METER req_0a9d3f2e chunk_index=3 tokens=598 event_id=evt_ab12
EMIT_METER req_0a9d3f2e chunk_index=3 tokens=598 event_id=evt_ab13
```
Both within ~120ms. Looks like identical chunk_index — event dedup didn't fire. I suspect the proxy caused the runtime to think the write failed and retried, but the metering producer didn't check for idempotency when re-emitting.

samir: customer notes this only impacts a minority of streaming sessions, but when it happens the invoice delta is very visible. They asked for temporary mitigation while we fix it.

ian: mitigation options: 1) Billing: ignore duplicate events with same req+chunk_index in 5s window (quick fix in metering pipeline). 2) Runtime: ensure emit is idempotent - only ack metering once per chunk index. 3) Recommend customers avoid transparent SSE proxies or enable proxy behavior to buffer rather than close on client disconnect.

marta: billing prefers (1) short-term while eng ships (2). Can you estimate risk of false suppression if chunk_index legitimately retries with different tokens?

ian: low. If tokens differ the chunk content hash would differ; we can require identical token_count + sha256(payload) to dedupe. That reduces false positives. I can PR a filter for the metering pipeline today.

samir: I'll tell the customer we're prioritizing this and ask if they can forward proxy config (nginx lua). Also asked if they can test a small patch: add header X-Stream-Id to preserve request id across reconnects.

support-bot: note: customer requested temporary invoice hold for INV-2026-09 until reconciliation complete.

marta: ack, placing invoice on hold for 72h. Ian, can you drop a link to the PR/issue when available and mark P1 for runtime dedupe?

ian: creating issue IR-1427 and draft PR in eng-runtime. Will add metering pipeline filter with sha256 compare and 5s window. ETA: 24-36h for PR, 3-5d for runtime rollout.

samir: thanks — I'll update the customer and ask for proxy config + whether they can reproduce against a direct call (no proxy).

marta: cc @billing-ops: monitor for similar invoice disputes, we may need to backfill a handful in last 30 days.

samir: summary for the thread: probable double-count caused by final chunk replay on reconnect -> runtime emitted duplicate metering events -> invoice double-count. Short-term billing dedupe + invoice hold. Long-term runtime idempotency.

ian: attaching quick query to find similar cases: 
```
SELECT req_id, COUNT(*) as emits, SUM(tokens) as tokens_sum
FROM metering_events
WHERE chunk_index IS NOT NULL AND timestamp > now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY req_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > (SELECT MAX(chunk_index)+1 FROM some_reference) -- heuristic
LIMIT 50;
```
samir: perfect. I'll follow up with the customer and paste the query results when we find matches. :thumbsup:
